terms.comment: verbum dēfectīvum: ōdī, pudet (Traupman 230). Traupman’s pupil explains: quia haec verba quibusdam figūrīs egent, because these verbs lack certain forms. Quintilian describes such words as those that cāsibus careant, lack cases (1.6.25).

phrases.latin: quaedam plūrāliter nōn dīcantur, quaedam contrā singulārī numerō, quaedam cāsibus careant
phrases.english: some are not used in the plural, some on the other hand not in the singular, some lack cases

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 230, 246.
Quintilian checked against the Perseus Latin texts, and cited by its numbering.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
